transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04 14:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez, Ethan Cole, Maya Liu (Redwood); Tom Hsu, Priya Patel, Daniel Ruiz, Lara Berg (Arcadia)
---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, rolling call, we'll try to keep this to an hour. quick status: we ran the INT8 and FP8 blends across the trident-3b-ish variant overnight, results are in. Ethan you want to kick us off with the numbers?
[00:18] Ethan: Yeah sure. so baseline (fp16) avg p50 token-latency on Arcadia workload was 42ms, INT8 blend dropped that to 30ms (-28%), FP8 gave 26ms (-38%). throughput improved similarly, about 1.7x for INT8, 2.1x FP8 on the long-tail batches.
[00:37] Tom: sorry quick q — are those numbers with KV cache enabled? we tested a few permutations and saw bigger wins when prefix caching was on.
[00:45] Ethan: Good call, these numbers are without KV prefix caching, full warm start. We have a second column in the spreadsheet where the cache-on numbers show smaller marginal latency because cache already saves tokens. cache-on + FP8 gave p50 18ms on short-turns in our local harness.
[01:05] Daniel: That sounds great on perf — but we saw a regression on long-form summarization for about 4% decrease in QA pass rate with INT8 and 6% with FP8 on our internal eval.
[01:17] Maya: Right — we dug into the examples, the failures cluster around rare entity preservation and numeric fidelity, especially multi-paragraph medical notes where tokenization boundaries matter. Some of it looks like quantization noise, some looks like beam search probabilities shifting.
[01:36] Priya: can you explain beam search probs shiffting a bit? I heard that during the last eng sync and not sure how much we can tune that.
[01:45] Ethan: Yep, quantization changes logits scale; with FP8 the dynamic range is different so the softmax temperature effectively shifts. You can tune sampling or temperature, use per-channel quant scales, or float-stash the final layer. There are a bunch of knobs.
[02:03] Lara: We need to prioritize; for production our SLA is conservative on hallucinations for clinical summaries. even a 4% drop is material for us.
[02:12] Sofia: Totally understood. This is why the pilot's hybrid strategy matters — we can route high-risk prompts to fp16 or a conservative INT8 profile, keep high-throughput traffic on FP8. The orchestration can be by prompt pattern or by customer route.
[02:29] Tom: how noisy are these numbers? confident they're not just dataset fluke?
[02:34] Ethan: We've run 3 seeds, CI gives similar deltas; the long-form examples are lower frequency but consistent. we'll push more samples from Arcadia to be sure.
[02:46] Priya: A security/compliance aside — we need traceability on model versions and quant profiles, and audit logs for any fallback decisions. Is that on the private control plane or the hosted API?
[02:58] Maya: For your Dedicated/Private setup we can enable the audit hooks; every routed request gets metadata with model_version, quant_profile, decision_reason. those logs can stream to your SIEM. We did note the KMS key rotations, though — sometimes encryption at rest metadata loses a little context in our ETL; we'll include the mapping doc.
[03:20] Daniel: Back to quality, any low-effort mitigations we can try before a rollback?
[03:27] Ethan: A few: 1) apply per-layer mixed precision — keep final 2 layers fp16; 2) per-channel scale calibration using your in-domain corpus; 3) increase beam/temperature conservative settings for summarization prompts; 4) selective routing: detect long-form summary intents and route to fp16.
[03:48] Sofia: For the POC I recommend a staged plan: replay 48h of production traffic with caching enabled and the FP8 profile, collect end-to-end QA metrics; in parallel run an INT8 run with mixed final layers to compare.
[04:02] Tom: Does replay require special infra from our side?
[04:07] Maya: No, you provide anonymized traffic or a 48h sample we run in the Redwood sandbox tethered to your VPC, or we can run locally with synthetic substitution. We will not persist PII; we have the redact pipeline.
[04:20] Daniel: We'll need to sign off on data handling — Priya will own that.
[04:25] Priya: Yup, we'll confirm consent and privacy gates.
[04:29] [05:00] Ethan: Quick note on tail latency — FP8 improved p99 by ~14% in our lab but on Arcadia's cloudy long-tail infra there was an anomaly: a few requests spiked due to GPU kernel fallback on mixed sequences. We're investigating kernel scheduling and cudnn/matmul dispatch thresholds.
[05:20] Tom: Are those kernel fallbacks something Redwood sees often?
[05:24] Ethan: Not common. happens when sequence length distribution is bimodal and the kernel chooser flips to a slower plan for certain lengths. We can fix by forcing a particular matmul plan or by fragmenting long sequences into stable chunks prior to inference.
[05:42] Lara: About budget — the FP8 delta looks great but what's the cost implication if we keep fp16 for 10% of high-risk traffic?
[05:50] Sofia: Our back-of-envelope: overall tokens cost down ~40% with 90% traffic on FP8 and 10% fp16. If you keep 20% fp16 cost reduction drops to ~30% but still a net win. We will produce a per-route cost table.
[06:06] Daniel: Ok, can we see a concrete rollback playbook? we need clear triggers and steps.
[06:12] Ethan: Yes — proposed playbook: 1) threshold breach detection (QA pass rate drop > 3% over 1h or hallucination metric > X), 2) auto-fallback to INT8-mixed, 3) if still bad, move traffic to fp16, 4) notify on-call and open incident. we'll provide the automation snippets.
[06:31] Priya: Do we get audit trails for the automated fallback? must be queryable for a compliance audit.
[06:37] Maya: Yes, decision logs include timeline and metric triggers, all stored with request IDs and model tags. we'll show a sample export.
[06:46] Sofia: On the evaluation front, Daniel — can you confirm the 2k-case eval includes 300 long-form clinical summaries and a stratified sample across languages?
[06:55] Daniel: I can do that, we'll include 350 long-forms to be safe and a 10% non-English stratification.
[07:03] Lara: Are we comfortable with the FP8 numeric stability on numerics-heavy notes? this was where we saw divergence.
[07:11] Ethan: The numeric fidelity issues are regular with lower precision. mitigation: maintain float stash for numeric tokens, use per-token weighting in calibration, or apply post-processing linter that verifies numeric consistency.
[07:28] Tom: Nice. Anything else on infra tweaks?
[07:31] Maya: We recommend enabling continuous batching but with conservative max-batch to avoid p99 spikes; also set autoscaling cooldowns to 45s to reduce jitter.
[07:42] Sofia: Also, we found one small bug in the routing policy UI that mislabels an INT8 variant as "low-precision-1" — we'll patch, but fine to operate manually until the fix.
[07:54] Priya: Can you guys send over the security and SOC-2 excerpts? we need those attached to the SSO docs.
[07:58] Sofia: Yes, will share SOC2 summary + KMS mapping and how audit logs surface; Maya will attach the mapping doc.
[08:08] Ethan: back to numbers, one more nuance — FP8 had slightly lower entropy outputs on creative prompts which actually reduced hallucination in some cases. so it's not all tradeoff negative.
[08:22] Daniel: Interesting — do you have examples where FP8 improved quality?
[08:26] Ethan: We have a small bucket where outputs were more conservative; will share the diff set.
[08:31] Lara: that's useful, we might tune decision logic to prefer FP8 for certain templates.
[08:36] Sofia: Alright, quick recap of concrete items: Redwood uploads quant profiles and runbook; Arcadia provides eval set; run replays; then we schedule canary. any objections?
[08:49] Tom: none from me.
[08:51] Priya: good.
[08:53] Daniel: no objections.
[08:55] Sofia: ok we'll aim to have the first replay by 2026-11-09 and a canary scheduled the following week. thanks everyone.
[09:05] [End of transcript]
notes: Transcript contains typical ASR imperfections: some product names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., K-V cash, Trident 3-B). Shared artifacts referenced: quant-profiles.xlsx (link), arcadia-evalset-2k.csv (link), replay-runbook.md (link), SOC2-summary.pdf (link).
